{{nihongo|'''Omura Shrine'''|大村神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Iga Province]].

'''Deity enshrined''

=== About the enshrined deity ===
The enshrined deity is listed as 1 in ``{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=God name book}}. On the other hand, in the ``Kofukuji Kanjusho'' written in the first year of {{ill|Kakitsu|Q1193238|qid=Q1193238}} ({{ill|1441|Q6402|qid=Q6402}}), ``Omurakami It is written as "Niza", and {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|Q11088805|qid=Q11088805}} was born in {{ill|Jingo-keiun|de|Jingo-Keiun|es|Jingo-keiun|fa|جینگو-کیئون|fr|Ère Jingo-keiun|ia|Jingo-keiun|id|Jingo-keiun|ja|神護景雲|ko|진고케이운|ru|Дзинго-кэйун|simple|Jingo-keiun|sr|Џинго кеиун|tr|Jingo-keiun|uk|Дзінґо Кей'ун|zh|神護景雲|zh_yue|神護景雲|qid=Q1373049}} in 2nd year ({{ill|768|Q29961|qid=Q29961}}). It is said to be the place where he rested when he moved from Jingu Shrine | Q706499}} to {{ill|Mikasayama|Q10866570|qid=Q10866570}} ({{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Q714559|qid=Q714559}}) {{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. The current enshrined deities are {{ill|Takemikazuchi|lt=Takemikazuchi|Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|Q1107286|qid=Q1107286|lt=Tsunetsu no Mikoto}}, {{jalin k|Amagiya-no-Mikoto|Q2564508|Amagoyane-no-Mikoto}} and the other three Kasuga deities originate from this transfer tradition, but its historical reality is unclear {{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}.On the other hand, {{ill|Prince Ikobayawake no Mikoto|Q11492324|qid=Q11492324}}, who is currently designated as Omura-kami, is a person whose relationship with the Abo area can be seen in ancient historical materials {{Sfn|Omura-jinja Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. First of all, in the article "{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399|qid=Q611399}}" dated November 21, {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 3rd year ({{ill|784|Q30083|qid=Q30083}}), the speed of breathing is {{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Gods)|1986}} who lived in Abo Village, Iga Province, and whose fourth grandson, King Sune Tsuto (Suchin Tsuto King), was given the surname "{{ill|Abo clan|Q11657230|qid=Q11657230|lt=Abo-kun}}". Also, “{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}” by Ukyo Emperor In the Abo Ason Article, it is written that Emperor Suinin created a palace in Abo Village, Iga Province and granted it to Isokubetsu no Mikoto as a fief, and that his descendants became Abo Ason ({{ill|Abo clan|Q11657230|qid=Q11657230}}) {{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. Near Omura Shrine, there is also a tomb designated by the Imperial Household Agency, which according to recent archeology dates back to {{ill|6th century|Q8090|qid=Q8090}}, so there is a theory that one of the tombs (Miyayama Tumulus Group) within the precincts of Omura Shrine is the tomb of Seisokubetsu no Mikoto.{{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Gods)|1986}}.In addition to the above, there is also a theory that the enshrined deity is Yuki Isun or Daimyo Somei ({{ill|Ōmura Clan (Shinbetsu)|Q11436025|qid=Q11436025|lt=Nao Omura}} ancestor) {{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. The 17 deities enshrined together are the 28 shrines of the former Abo town and 3 shrines of the former Taneo village that were enshrined between 1890 and 1986 ({{ill|1890|Q7832|qid=Q7832}}-{{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}}).

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
Founding date is unknown. As mentioned above, there is a legend about the transfer of Kasuga God from 2 years {{ill|Jingo-keiun|de|Jingo-Keiun|es|Jingo-keiun|fa|جینگو-کیئون|fr|Ère Jingo-keiun|ia|Jingo-keiun|id|Jingo-keiun|ja|神護景雲|ko|진고케이운|ru|Дзинго-кэйун|simple|Jingo-keiun|sr|Џинго кеиун|tr|Jingo-keiun|uk|Дзінґо Кей'ун|zh|神護景雲|zh_yue|神護景雲|qid=Q1373049}} ({{ill|768|Q29961|qid=Q29961}}) (first seen in historical sources is {{ill|1441|Q6402|qid=Q6402}}) ), there is a theory that assumes the involvement of the {{ill|Abo clan|Q11657230|qid=Q11657230}} (a descendant clan of the Breathless Gods) who made this place {{ill|Korean clans|Q846706|qid=Q846706}}{{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. Regarding the company's name, there is a theory that it is a corruption of ``Omori'', which refers to a group of shrines, to ``Omura'', since it looks like ``Omori Shrine/Omori Myojin'' in ancient times, or that it is a corruption of the place name ``Abo Village'', which is a corruption of ``Omura'', but the name is unknown.{{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Gods)|1986}}.

Furthermore, the Akinaga clan had been in charge of the Shinto priesthood since Tensho 15 (1990).After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, on August 7, {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 17 ({{ill|1884|Q7819|qid=Q7819}}), he was ranked as {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} in {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern Company Ranking System}}, and in Meiji 39 In December 2006 ({{ill|1906|Q2049|qid=Q2049}}), it was designated as a Shinto shrine, and in 5 years ({{j alink|1930|Q18787}}) On November 27th, it was promoted to {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=prefectural shrine|qid=Q90139226}}. {{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Shikiuchi)|1990}}. {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}} was once a Zenjoji temple, but it was abandoned in the first year of the Meiji era {{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}.

=== God level ===
* {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} 5th year ({{ill|863|Q25052|qid=Q25052}}) March 16th, from upper 6th rank to lower junior fifth rank (``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'') - Written as ``Omurakami.''

=== Precincts ===
The current ``main shrine'' was built in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}23 ({{ill|1890|Q7832|qid=Q7832}}){{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. It is {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|es|Kasuga-zukuri|fr|Kasuga-zukuri|ja|春日造|ru|Касуга-дзукури|qid=Q3193781}}, and the roof is {{ill|cypress bark roof|ja|檜皮葺|zh|檜皮葺|qid=Q90373477}}.{{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1990}}.

The old main hall, which was used before the current main hall, is adjacent to the west side of the current main hall as the ``Hoden''. This Hoden was built in the 15th year of {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ckb|تێنشۆ (سەردەمی مۆمۆیاما)|fa|تنشو|fr|Ère Tenshō (Momoyama)|ja|天正|ko|덴쇼 (아즈치모모야마 시대)|ro|Era Tenshō (Momoyama)|ru|Тэнсё (Адзути-Момояма)|simple|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|sr|Теншо (Момојама период)|sv|Tenshō|tr|Tenshō (Momoyama)|zh|天正 (日本)|qid=Q1145058}} ({{ill|1587|ab|1587|af|1587|als|1587|am|1587 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1587|ar|1587|ary|1587|arz|1587|ast|1587|avk|1587|az|1587|azb|۱۵۸۷ (میلادی)|bar|1587|bcl|1587|be|1587|be_x_old|1587|bg|1587|bn|১৫৮৭|bpy|মারি ১৫৮৭|br|1587|bs|1587.|ca|1587|cdo|1587 nièng|ceb|1587|ckb|١٥٨٧|crh|1587|cs|1587|cv|1587|cy|1587|da|1587|de|1587|diq|1587|el|1587|eml|1587|eo|1587|es|1587|et|1587|eu|1587|fa|۱۵۸۷ (میلادی)|fi|1587|fo|1587|fr|1587|frr|1587|fur|1587|fy|1587|ga|1587|gan|1587年|gcr|1587|gd|1587|gl|1587|he|1587|hi|१५८७|hr|1587.|ht|1587 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1587|hy|1587|hyw|1587 թուական|ia|1587|id|1587|ilo|1587|io|1587|is|1587|it|1587|ja|1587年|jv|1587|ka|1587|kaa|1587|kk|1587 жыл|ko|1587년|krc|1587 джыл|la|1587|lb|1587|lij|1587|lmo|1587|lt|1587 m.|lv|1587. gads|mai|१५८७|map_bms|1587|mdf|1587|mg|1587|mhr|1587|mi|1587|mk|1587|mr|इ.स. १५८७|mrj|1587 и|ms|1587|my|၁၅၈၇|mzn|۱۵۸۷|nah|1587|nap|1587|nds|1587|new|सन् १५८७|nl|1587|nn|1587|no|1587|nrm|1587|nso|1587|oc|1587|or|୧୫୮୭|os|1587-æм аз|pa|1587|pl|1587|pnb|1587|pt|1587|qu|1587|ro|1587|ru|1587 год|rue|1587|sa|१५८७|sah|1587|scn|1587|sd|1587ع|se|1587|sh|1587.|shn|1587|simple|1587|sk|1587|sl|1587|smn|1587|sq|1587|sr|1587|su|1587|sv|1587|sw|1587|ta|1587|te|1587|tg|Соли 1587|th|พ.ศ. 2130|tk|1587|tl|1587|tly|1587|tr|1587|tt|1587 ел|uk|1587|ur|1587ء|uz|1587|vec|1587|vi|1587|vls|1587|wa|1587|war|1587|wuu|1587年|xmf|1587|yi|1587|zh|1587年|zh_min_nan|1587 nî|zh_yue|1587年|qid=Q6744}}) of the {{ill|Azuchi–Momoyama period|Q319531|qid=Q319531}}.<ref name="Hoden"/> Ikkensha {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}}, with a tsumairi roof, {{ill|cypress bark roof|ja|檜皮葺|zh|檜皮葺|qid=Q90373477}}<ref name="Hoden"/>. It is said that the form as well as the carvings and coloring remain as they were at the time of construction, and it has been designated as a national {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|de|Wichtiges Kulturgut Japans|es|Bien Cultural Importante de Japón|fi|Japanin tärkeä kulttuuriomaisuus|fr|Bien culturel important|id|Properti Kebudayaan Penting (Jepang)|it|Bene culturale importante (Giappone)|ja|重要文化財|ko|일본의 중요문화재|ro|Patrimoniu cultural important al Japoniei|simple|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|th|ทรัพย์สินทางวัฒนธรรมที่สำคัญ (ญี่ปุ่น)|tr|Önemli Kültürel Varlık (Japonya)|uk|Важливі культурні пам'ятки Японії|zh|重要文化財|qid=Q1188622}}<ref name="Hoden"/>.In addition, within the precincts there is a {{ill|Kaname-ishi|Q11630053|qid=Q11630053}}, which is worshiped as a spiritual stone, and the strange bell ``Mushikui-kane'' {{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. The name "Insect-eaten bell" comes from the fact that the bumps on its surface fell off due to a chemical change, but it was originally a temple bell at Zenjoji Temple (formerly Bettoji Temple) and was completed in {{ill|Meireki|Q1192766|qid=Q1192766}}2 ({{ill|1656|Q6982|qid=Q6982}}) {{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. Also, from the approach to the shrine grounds to the vicinity of the shrine building, there are several {{ill|Round Kofun|Q11394747|qid=Q11394747}} known as the ``Miyayama kofun group''{{Sfn|Omura Shrine (Gods)|1986}}.

=== Festival ===
List of festivals held annually at Omura Shrine <ref name="Yoshisho"/>.
*Monthly festival (1st day of every month)
* Saitan Festival (New Year's Day Festival) (January 1st)
* First prayer (during New Year)
* Prayer festival to ward off evil spirits (February 1st)
* Prayer to ward off evil spirits (January to end of February)
* Prayer Festival (February 21st)
* Spring Festival (April 10th)
* Eireisha Festival (August 15th)
* Earthquake disaster prevention prayer festival (September 1st)
* Jugoya Festival (Jūgoya Festival)
*Autumn Festival (November 2nd and 3rd)
* Shichi-Go-San prayer (during November)
* New Grain Thanksgiving (November 21st)
* New Year's Eve Bell (New Year's Eve)
